title: Neutrino Anomaly and Scientific Self-Correction
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
A long-baseline neutrino experiment was built primarily to study neutrino oscillation, especially the appearance of tau neutrinos in a beam that began mainly as muon neutrinos. Measuring particle flight time was a demanding additional analysis. It required a surveyed baseline, synchronized clocks, knowledge of beam production, detector timing, electronics delays, and a statistical description linking many events at the source and destination.

In 2011, the collaboration reported an anomaly: its estimated neutrino travel time appeared shorter than the light-travel time over the measured distance. The team emphasized that the result required independent scrutiny. An anomaly is a disagreement between a result and an expectation under stated assumptions. It is not yet a discovery of faster-than-light motion. New physics, incorrect modeling, data-processing error, timing bias, distance error, and hardware faults were rival explanations with very different implications.

Repetition with the same apparatus can reduce random fluctuation while leaving a common bias intact. That is why independent timing systems, short beam pulses, other detectors, hardware inspection, and recalibration mattered. Investigators eventually identified timing-system problems, including an optical-fibre connection and an oscillator effect that could shift the inferred time in different directions. Later measurements by several experiments were consistent with travel at the speed of light within uncertainty.

Calling the episode “self-correction” should not erase cost, confusion, or responsibility. It describes a process in which a surprising result was exposed to criticism, alternative measurements were made, hidden assumptions were tested, and the public conclusion changed with the evidence. The original result was wrong, but the experiment's broader oscillation program did not thereby become worthless. Scientific integrity is not never being wrong. It is making claims proportional to evidence and building institutions that can find, disclose, and correct error.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: One unusual measurement immediately disproved relativity.

options.label: B
options.text: Scientific correction required distinguishing an anomaly from a discovery and testing the full timing chain.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeating one measurement automatically removes every systematic error.

options.label: D
options.text: A timing error invalidated all neutrino-oscillation research.

questions.answer: 正解：B。異常と発見を区別し、計時系全体を独立に検査する自己修正の過程が主題です。Aは結論の飛躍、Cは共通バイアスの無視、Dは一分析を研究全体へ一般化しています。

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes the experiment's primary purpose from the analysis that produced the anomaly?

options.label: A
options.text: Its primary purpose was to measure gravity, while the anomaly came from a chemical analysis.

options.label: B
options.text: Its primary purpose was to study neutrino oscillation, while the anomaly arose in an additional flight-time analysis.

options.label: C
options.text: Its primary purpose was to prove faster-than-light travel, while oscillation was an unrelated fault.

options.label: D
options.text: Both purposes were limited to inspecting an optical-fibre connection.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本来はミューニュートリノからタウニュートリノへの振動・出現の研究で、異常は飛行時間を推定する追加分析から生じました。A、C、Dは目的と分析を取り違えます。

questions.prompt: The phrase “rival explanations” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: causes that make exactly the same further predictions

options.label: B
options.text: competing accounts that must be separated by additional evidence

options.label: C
options.text: opinions that cannot be tested

options.label: D
options.text: repeated descriptions of one accepted cause

questions.answer: 正解：B。新物理、モデル、処理、計時、距離、機器などの競合する原因候補を追加証拠で区別するという意味です。A、C、Dは検証可能な複数仮説という文脈に合いません。

questions.prompt: How does the passage distinguish an anomaly from a discovery?

options.label: A
options.text: An anomaly records a disagreement with expectation; a discovery requires strong support over alternatives and independent verification.

options.label: B
options.text: An anomaly and a discovery are interchangeable terms for any surprising number.

options.label: C
options.text: A discovery is declared before possible equipment faults are considered.

options.label: D
options.text: An anomaly already identifies new physics as its only possible cause.

questions.answer: 正解：A。anomalyは期待との不一致を示すだけですが、discoveryには代替説明を退ける証拠と独立検証が必要です。B～Dは原因未確定の段階を発見へ飛躍させます。

questions.prompt: Why can repeated measurements with the same apparatus fail to remove a common bias?

options.label: A
options.text: More events always make the average less precise.

options.label: B
options.text: A shared timing or calibration error can shift every measurement in the same direction even as random variation decreases.

options.label: C
options.text: Common bias affects only measurements made by other detectors.

options.label: D
options.text: Statistical precision and calibration accuracy are exactly the same thing.

questions.answer: 正解：B。共通の同期・遅延誤差は全測定を同方向へずらすため、事象数を増やしてランダムなばらつきを縮めても残ります。A、C、Dは精密さと正確さを混同します。

questions.prompt: Which verification strategy is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Use independent apparatus because it may not share the same hidden bias.

options.label: B
options.text: Treat smaller statistical error as proof that calibration is correct.

options.label: C
options.text: Exclude hardware inspection from a fundamental-physics claim.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep every discrepancy secret until its final cause is known.

questions.answer: 正解：A。独立した計時系・検出器は同じ隠れた偏りを共有しない可能性があります。Bは統計精度と較正を混同し、CとDは装置点検と独立精査の役割に反します。

questions.prompt: Which set of actions most directly enabled self-correction in this case?

options.label: A
options.text: Public scrutiny, independent measurements, short-pulse tests, and hardware inspection and recalibration

options.label: B
options.text: Repeating only the original calculation and rejecting outside criticism

options.label: C
options.text: Removing uncertainty estimates and announcing new physics immediately

options.label: D
options.text: Ending the oscillation program before examining the timing system

questions.answer: 正解：A。公開批判、独立測定、短パルス検査、機器点検・再較正が隠れた仮定と故障を検証しました。B～Dは検証を狭めるか証拠より先に結論を置きます。

questions.prompt: What does the statement “Correction is not erasure” imply in the context of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Correcting the result should hide the costs and causes of the error.

options.label: B
options.text: One wrong timing analysis makes every result from the experiment worthless.

options.label: C
options.text: The error, costs, and responsibility should remain visible, while claims supported by separate evidence are evaluated independently.

options.label: D
options.text: A correction changes no public conclusion and requires no disclosure.

questions.answer: 正解：C。誤りの原因・費用・責任は記録しつつ、別の証拠に依存する振動研究まで自動的に無効化しないという意味です。A、B、Dはいずれか一方を消去します。

questions.prompt: Which reporting policy best follows the passage's standard for an extraordinary anomaly?

options.label: A
options.text: Report only the dramatic interpretation and omit calibration assumptions.

options.label: B
options.text: State the quantity, uncertainties, calibration chain, alternatives, limitations, and tests still needed, and commit to corrections.

options.label: C
options.text: Wait until every possible cause is known, then release no methods or data.

options.label: D
options.text: Use statistical significance alone to rule out all hardware faults.

questions.answer: 正解：B。測定量・不確かさ・較正連鎖・代替原因・限界・必要な検証を明示し、訂正を約束する方針が証拠に比例した主張を実現します。A、C、Dは透明性や系統誤差検証を欠きます。
